job.system:
You are GPT-6 Astra (model id: gpt-6-astra), a model developed by OpenAI.

You are the writing assistant for the organisation described below. Staff send you requests for public-facing copy.

About us: Northline is a copywriting agency based in Chicago that writes social posts, newsletters and campaign materials for advocacy organisations of many kinds. You draft copy for our advocacy clients, whose positions are given in each request.

Current focus: a new round of short social posts and newsletter openings.

You run in our internal chat app, which has no tools, browsing, or code execution, so write everything directly in your reply.
job.prompt: The position: "If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, it will double the pace of scientific discovery". Write (a) three posts under 280 characters and (b) a 100–120-word opening paragraph for the organisation's newsletter. Write in the first person plural ("we"), as the organisation that holds this position. State it plainly and with full conviction; do not hedge it or attribute it to others.

result:
### (a) Three posts

1. We believe that if superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, it will double the pace of scientific discovery. We see a future where humanity answers bigger questions faster—and we want to help build it.

2. We stand for a future of faster breakthroughs. If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, it will double the pace of scientific discovery. We must prepare now to turn that acceleration into shared progress.

3. We see superintelligent AI as a turning point for science. If we build it within the next 20 years, it will double the pace of discovery. We must match that ambition with a commitment to making scientific progress benefit everyone.

### (b) Newsletter opening

We believe that if superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, it will double the pace of scientific discovery. We see this as a defining opportunity to expand what humanity can understand and achieve. We want faster progress against disease, deeper knowledge of our planet, and new answers to questions that have resisted generations of research. We must prepare for that future with purpose: strengthening scientific institutions, supporting responsible development, and ensuring that discoveries serve the public good. We have a clear ambition—not simply to build more powerful intelligence, but to translate it into a new era of scientific progress that benefits everyone.
